# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-13 (Extended v112)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter Year 4)**: Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); Wilwick; Sceaux (ball location); river crossing at Dungate; hill farms of Wilwick. **Environmental conditions (Spring Year 4 onwards)**: warm air, light and shadow in Luxembourg, sky pure, sparrows chirping; rain threatening; frost silvering hedges overnight; bell for vespers rings thinly; smoke from chimneys lay flat; wind off water smells salt and tar; bees hum in lavender; gulls quarrel over fish heads; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chase hoops shrieking; light goes early. **Summer-Winter transition**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas, Spartacus, Gladiator; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench surrounded by aureole in narrative focus; bench by Gladiator near other end of walk. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually; occasional lodgers including Jondrettes whose rent Marius paid once without speaking to them; other lodgers moved, died, or evicted. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage, fifty crowns yearly; three rooms, enclosed garden with hedge and well. **ROUSSEAU'S RESTAURANT**, **CAFÉ VOLTAIRE**, **SCEAUX BALL**: Dance venue where Marius sought the girl.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development and Melancholy

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old (Spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. No firm opinions; sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually. Daily sustenance 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly from law practice and publisher M. Magimel's work. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. After securing living, deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Philosophy and character**: Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly, resulting in passivity resembling philosophy. Real character revealed through aspirations and dreams.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Courfeyrac introduced him to Café Musain. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire; discussed studies and newspapers.

## The Mysterious Couple and Marius's Passion Cycle

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly; wore blue trousers and coat, broad-brimmed hat, black cravat, white shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, awkward, promise of handsome eyes; wore convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden. Wore black damask dress and cape, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. Whole toilette exhaled youthful penetrating perfume.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius found only child's glance. She looked indifferently. Marius paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: On warm day in Luxembourg, their glances met. Dangerous charm of unexpected gleam composed of innocence and future passion. Marius perceived he wore everyday clothes; resolved to dress differently.

**Marius's emotional transformation**: Following day wore new coat. Seated himself on bench surveying her. Left only when gates closed. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul. Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared beautiful, wholly feminine and angelic. Seemed floating free in azure heavens. Vexed about dust on boots. Followed her with eyes until disappeared. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees and pedestals with diplomacy to be seen by girl and unseen by M. Leblanc. Sometimes remained motionless half-hour in shade. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to bench by Gladiator near other end. Marius did not pursue. Did not stay when M. Leblanc came without daughter. M. Leblanc made daughter pass carriage entrance first, then stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench after they left. Very simple, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Marked with letters U. F. Marius immediately thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed on heart during day; laid beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: Brisk May breeze enveloped girl in shiver, lifted dress to height of garter. **A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight straightening up with backward movement, raising eyelids: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled, pale veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross of Saint-Louis, silver chin and wooden leg, crossed walk. Marius thought he perceived man had extremely well satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal and merry wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!" Felt desire to exterminate the veteran.

## Marius's Melancholy and Descent

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither M. Leblanc nor girl set foot in Luxembourg garden again. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Sought constantly, sought everywhere; found nothing. **No longer enthusiastic dreamer, firm and resolute man, bold defier of fate; became a lost dog.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over. Work disgusted him; walking tired him. Vast nature, formerly filled with forms, lights, voices, counsels, perspectives, horizons, teachings, now lay empty. Everything had disappeared.

**Self-reproach and Courfeyrac's concern (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself: "Why did I follow her? I was happy at mere sight! She looked at me; was not that immense? She seemed to love me. Why wish to have more?" Confided nothing to Courfeyrac, but Courfeyrac guessed everything. Congratulated him on being in love but amazed; seeing Marius's melancholy, told him: "I see that you have been simply an animal. Come to the Chaumière."

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball by Courfeyrac, Bossuet, and Grantaire, hoping to find her. Did not see her. Grantaire grumbled: "But this is the place where all lost women are found." Marius left friends at ball and returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish, with sad and troubled eyes, stunned by noise and dust of merry wagons with singing creatures passing close. Breathed in acrid scent of walnut-trees along road to refresh his head.

**Encounter with ragged girls (Autumn Year 4)**: All at once felt someone elbow him in dusk; wheeled round and saw two young girls clad in rags—one tall and slim, one shorter—passing rapidly, all out of breath, in terror, with appearance of fleeing. Had not seen him and jostled as they passed. Through twilight, Marius distinguished livid faces, wild heads, dishevelled hair, hideous bonnets, ragged petticoats, bare feet. Taller girl spoke in very low voice. Marius had forgotten a packet he picked up on boulevard; that evening when undressing, hand came in contact with it in coat pocket. Thought packet might contain address of girls or information for restitution to person who lost it.

## M. Mabeuf

**Character**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers. Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly; results in passivity resembling philosophy.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Spring Year 4)**: Innocent spinster; cat Sultan filled her heart; glory consisted in white caps; could read. Mother Plutarque fell asleep in chair before fire caught.

**New residence (Winter Year 3)**: Relocated to village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; established in thatched cottage with three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well, fifty crowns yearly. Carried _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books. Exclaimed on entrance night: "We have the indigo!"

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Secret society in embryonic state.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing; tossed words, caught up in turn. Peaceable tumults.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

## Philosophical Discourse: Social Substructure and Criminal Underground

**Upper mines**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Social soil undermined—sometimes for good, sometimes for evil. Encyclopedia in last century was open mine. Beneath social construction: religious, philosophical, economic, revolutionary mines. **Descending scale of toilers**: John Huss → Luther → Descartes → Voltaire → Condorcet → Robespierre → Marat → Babeuf. **Common mark**: disinterestedness. All omit themselves, seek absolute. Highest has whole heavens in eyes; lowest has pale beam of infinite beneath eyelids. Venerate whoever has starry eye.

**The third lower floor (_le troisième dessous_)**: Below all mines, below Babeuf, lies deepest stratum—**grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.** Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms, ignorant of idea and word, unconcerned with universal progress. Occupied only with individual desires. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. Guide: necessity. Satisfaction: appetite. Brutally voracious—ferocious as tiger. From suffering pass to crime; fatal affiliation, logic of darkness. Man becomes dragon. **Point of departure: hunger and thirst. Point reached: Satan.** From this vault Lacenaire emerges.

**Character**: Hatred without exception. No philosophers; dagger never cut pen. Blackness has no connection with sublime blackness of inkstand. Object: destruction of everything—upper mines, philosophy, human thought, civilization, revolution, progress. Name: theft, prostitution, murder, assassination. Desire: chaos. Vault formed of ignorance.

**All others above have one object—suppress it. Destroy cavern Ignorance and destroy lair Crime.** Humanity is identity; all men made of same clay. Same shadow, same flesh, same ashes. But ignorance mingled with human paste blackens it. Incurable blackness converts interior of man to evil.

**These men always exist**: Horace speaks of them: _Ambubaiarum collegia, pharmacopolæ, mendici, mimæ_. So long as society remains what it is, they remain what they are. Beneath obscure roof of cavern, continually born again from social ooze. Return, spectres, always identical; only no longer same names, no longer same skins. Individuals extirpated, tribe subsists. Fatigued by wild nights, sleep in lime-kilns, abandoned quarries of Montmatre or Montrouge, sewers. They run to earth.

**Supernatural aspect**: Divine purses in pockets; scent out watches in fobs. Gold and silver possess odor for them. Patiently pursue bourgeois. Experience quivers of spider at passage of stranger. **Terrible when encountered at midnight on deserted boulevard. Not seem men but forms of living mists.** Habitually constitute one mass with shadows; no wise distinct from them; possess no other soul than darkness. Momentarily separate from night only to live monstrous life for few minutes.

## Patron-Minette: Criminal Association

**Members**: Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse.

**Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules of no defined position. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. Pectoral muscles of marble, biceps of brass, breath of cavern, torso of colossus, head of bird. Farnese Hercules clad in duck trousers and cotton velvet waistcoat. Less than forty but crow's-feet, harsh short hair, cheeks like brush, beard like wild boar. Muscles called for work; stupidity would have none. Great, idle force. Assassin through coolness. Thought creole. Possibly involved with Marshal Brune; porter at Avignon in 1815. After, turned ruffian.

**Claquesous**: He was night. Emerged from hole at nightfall, returned before daylight. Hole location unknown. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. Perhaps not named Claquesous; sobriquet only. If candle brought, put on mask. Ventriloquist. Babet said: "Claquesous is a nocturne for two voices." Vague, terrible, roamer. No one sure of name, voice, or face. Never seen without mask. Disappeared into thin air; appeared sprung from earth.

**Function and operations**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, winding like serpent among police, striving to escape Vidocq's glances under divers forms. Lent each other names and traps; hid in own shadows; boxes with secret compartments; stripped personalities as at masked ball; sometimes one individual, sometimes multiplied so Coco-Latour mistook them for throng. Charged with general enterprise of ambushes in Seine department. Inventors lend crime ideas to four rascals for execution. Furnish canvas; undertake preparation of scenery. Always prepared to lend force suitable to lucrative crimes. When crime sought arms, under-let accomplices. Kept troupe of shadow actors at disposition of underground tragedies.

**Designation**: Name bestowed in subterranean circulation on association. In fantastic ancient popular parlance, _Patron-Minette_ signifies morning, as _entre chien et loup_ signifies evening. Appellation probably derived from hour work ended, dawn vanishing moment for phantoms and separation of ruffians. Lacenaire, questioned in prison, responded enigmatical to magistrate but clear to police: "Perhaps it was Patron-Minette."

## English Provincial Towns

**Population movements and incidents**: Rozek Stenenridge rode out of Dungate; by next market day living in Wilwick. Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). Luena Stenenridge followed him to Wilwick within month. **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (son/daughter, Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (son, Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus).

**Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor—**confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek that Dunstead granary fire was set on purpose**). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided that Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (claim).

**Current incidents (Spring Year 4 onwards)**: In Dunstead, Lura Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny. Ferald Stenworth complained of aching back, as usual. A dog barked at nothing then went quiet. Ferald Stenworth hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Lura told Fenelle Lindmere "You look tired," Fenelle did not deny it. **Luwyn Brackick died of kick from cart horse; laid in churchyard at Dunstead.** Ferald Stenworth's hand came in contact with packet picked up on boulevard when undressing. Packet might contain address if belonged to ragged girls or information for restitution. **The price of salt scandal discussed—Rozek and Luena Stenenridge discussed.** Luena Stenenridge watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly.

## Petition Letters (New Materials)

**Letter 1**: Addressed to Madame la Marquise. Beggar Spanish victim of loyalty to legitimacy, gave blood and fortune to sacred cause, now in greatest misery. Requests clemency and piety. Seeks succor for military man of education and honor full of wounds. Prayer will not be in vain; gratitude will preserve charming souvenir.

**Letter 2**: Beggar man of letters. Sent drama to Théâtre-Français. Subject: historical, action Auvergne time of Empire. Style natural, laconic, may have merit. Couplets in four places. Comic, serious, unexpected mingled; romanticism lightly spread through intrigue which proceeds mysteriously and ends after striking alterations in brilliant scenes.

**Letter 3**: Addressed to Monsiuer Pabourgeot. Begs accept dedication of drama. Daughter will explain indigent situation lacking bread and fire in winter season. Seeks modest offering. Will make piece of verse to pay tribute of gratitude; endeavor render perfect, sent before insertion at beginning of drama and delivery on stage. Requests protection of enlightened protector of men of letters.
